texts.arguments: Accused was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and caused death of rider and injuries to pillion rider. 26.Per contra, it is argued by the Ld. counsel for accused that there are material contradictions in testimony of witnesses. Prosecution has failed to prove rashness and negligence on part of the accused. No public witness is joined by the IO. Eyewitness has deposed falsely at the instance of IO.

annotations_dropped.text_preview: 25.It is argued by the state that prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Tempo has collided with motorcycle and one person has died, res ipsa loquitor is argued by the Ld. APP.
27.I have heard the state and accused and have perused the record carefully.

28. Allegations against the accused are for offence under section 279/338/304A IPC.
29.Section 279 IPC provides that Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to b

31.In a nutshell to prove the case against the accused the prosecution was under the obligation to prove the following essential ingredients of the offence punishable u/s 279/304A IPC :
a. Identity of the accused being the driver of the of
b. That the alleged accident is the result of rash and negligent driving of the accused at a public place. c. The rash and negligent driving of the accused resulted in the death of the deceased.
d. The rash and negligent driving of the accused resulted in the simple injury to the injured.

32. The question in this case is as to whether, on the evidence on record, it is proved that accused was driving the vehicle and whether he was driving in rash and negligent manner and whether death and injury was caused due to rash and neg

33.It was held in Niranjan Singh vs The State (Delhi Administration) 1997 CriLJ 336 that Rashness consists in CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 14 of 17 hazarding a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge tha
The criminality lies in such a case in running the risk of doing such an act with recklessness or indifference as to the consequences.

Criminal negligence on the other hand is the gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable or proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which hav

Thus, the main criterion for deciding whether the driving which led to the accident was rash and negligent is not only the speed of the offending vehicle but deliberate disregard to the obligation of its driver to drive with due care and at

In a case of this nature, the test is whether the prosecution has proved that :-
(i) the accused was driving the vehicle in such a manner as to create an obvious and serious risk of causing physical injury to some other person who might hap
present case
it is not disputed that accused was driving the vehicle but that he was driving in rash and negligent manner.
In present case prosecution has failed to prove that accused was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
There is no evidence on record to show that accused was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
Eye witness PW 7 has only deposed to the effect that offending vehicle was overtaking the vehicle and came from front side and hit the motorcycle.
However, version of witness do not corroborate with the mechanical inspection report.
AS per report offending vehicle was damaged from left side.
If accused had overtook the vehicle from right side and hit motorcycle from front then damage should have occurred at right side, and could not have hit the motorcycle at left.
As per site plan there is no divider on the place of incident.
Traffic direction is not shown on site plan.
It is not proved cogently, if accused or injured were on wrong side of the road.
PW 11 has stated that vehicle of injured was on wrong side of road.
Bald statement of witness that accused was rash and negligent will not ipso facto establish the fact.
35.It is admitted fact that Tempo stopped at the spot, if it was on very high speed, it would have been difficult to stop the same at the spot after the incident.
Further it is nowhere alleged that it was at high speed.
Moreover, It is already discussed rashness is not about high speed but total CC 5283953/16 State Vs. Kuldeep Singh FIR No. 264/11 PS Alipur 16 of 17 disregard of traffic rules and caution.
No such fact is brought on record to show that accused was driving in rash and negligent manner.

In the absence of any material on the record, no presumption of "rashness" or "negligence"
could be drawn by invoking the maxim "res ipsa loquitur".

36. Site plan on record is prepared on the day of incident, and signed by the injured, further IO has stated that he met injured on day of incident at the spot, however, PW 7 in his cross examination has stated that " I left the hospital a

37.IO has not joined the public witness despite availaibility, notice to join investigation was also not given by the IO to the public, such failure to join public witnesses, cast shadow of doubt on the prosecution case.
38.
In such circumstances, it cannot be said that prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, accused Kuldeep Singh is acquitted for offence under section 279/338/304A IPC.
